subject: Astronomy & Space
title: The Future of Cosmology
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Future of Cosmology usable.

hook.text: Cosmology has answered huge questions in just a century. The next decades promise even bigger breakthroughs.

buildup.text: JWST is peering deeper than ever. The Vera Rubin Observatory will survey billions of galaxies starting in 2025.

discovery.text: Gravitational wave detectors may soon hear echoes from the Big Bang itself—primordial ripples in spacetime.

twist.text: We still don't know what dark matter or dark energy is. Solving either would be the discovery of the century.

climax.text: Cosmology's biggest questions remain open: What triggered the Big Bang? Is the universe infinite? Are we alone?

punchline.text: A century of answers. An eternity of questions still ahead.

quiz.question: What major unsolved problem could transform cosmology if answered?
options: Identifying what dark matter and dark energy actually are
Determining the exact age of the Earth
Mapping every star in the Milky Way

details.summary: Cosmology's next frontiers include resolving the Hubble tension, understanding dark energy's true nature, detecting primordial gravitational waves from inflation, mapping the cosmic Dark Ages with 21-cm radio surveys, and searching for signs of the multiverse.
details.whyItMatters: The biggest questions in cosmology remain unanswered: What is dark energy? What is dark matter? Did inflation happen? Is there a multiverse? The next generation of instruments may finally crack these profound mysteries.
takeaways: Resolving the Hubble tension may reveal new physics
Dark energy and dark matter identification are top priorities
New telescopes will probe the earliest epochs of the universe

faq.question: What new instruments will advance cosmology?
faq.answer: The Vera C. Rubin Observatory will map the sky repeatedly, discovering transients and weak lensing. The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope will measure dark energy. LISA will detect gravitational waves from space. The Square Kilometre Array will map hydrogen across cosmic time.

faq.question: Could cosmology ever be 'complete'?
faq.answer: Unlikely. Each answered question reveals deeper mysteries. Understanding dark energy might reveal new physics, resolving the Hubble tension might overturn standard cosmology, and detecting inflation's signature might point toward a multiverse.
